title: Record visit progress, cancellation and no-shows
summary: Keep arrivals, service progress and appointment history accurate.

sections.title: Record what has happened
sections.body:
1. Open the visit from **Dashboard** or **Calendar**.
2. Check the client and service before using the available next action, such as confirmation, arrival, check-in, service start or completion.
3. Wait for the status to update before making another change.
4. After completion, open **Checkout** if payment needs recording and your role permits it.

Only transitions valid for the visit’s present state are offered. Completing an appointment does not mean its sale has been paid.

sections.title: Cancel a visit or record a no-show
sections.body:
1. Open the appointment in Calendar and choose its cancellation action.
2. In **Cancel this appointment?**, choose **Why is this appointment being cancelled?**. If you select **Other**, enter **Other reason**.
3. Check the client and time, then select **Cancel appointment**. Select **Keep appointment** to leave it unchanged.
4. If the client did not attend, use the no-show action and confirm **Mark no-show** instead.

Cancellation and a confirmed no-show release reserved time and retain history. A past scheduled time alone does not establish a no-show. Cancellation reasons distinguish client-requested and business cancellations in reports.

sections.title: Payments and notifications
sections.body:
Cancelling a visit does not prove that a deposit or payment was returned. Review payment records separately and follow the business’s cancellation policy.

Eligible status changes may create client notifications according to channel choices and consent. A saved appointment status is not proof that the client received the message; check **Client notifications → Delivery history** when delivery matters.
